definition: In artificial intelligence (AI) research, neuralese is a method where Large Language Models (LLMs) perform intermediate reasoning steps in their high-dimensional latent space (vector embeddings) rather than outputting human-readable text tokens.
details: While standard Chain of thought (AI) reasoning forces a model to generate a sequence of words, neuralese allows the model to pass raw, continuous vectors between computational layers, creating a high-bandwidth, non-linguistic reasoning channel.

explainer.lead: Neuralese is a method where LLMs perform intermediate reasoning steps in their high-dimensional latent space rather than emitting human-readable tokens. It creates a high-bandwidth, non-linguistic reasoning channel between computational layers.

tiers.eli5: Instead of thinking out loud in words, the model passes private shorthand notes to itself that no human reads, which carries more information per step.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use neuralese to pass raw continuous vectors between layers, aiming for higher-bandwidth reasoning than chain-of-thought text. The pitfall is that the intermediate reasoning is not human-readable, so it is harder to inspect and debug.
tiers.paperLevel: Intermediate reasoning is carried as continuous vectors in the model's embedding space rather than as discrete text tokens. Known limit: the reasoning channel is non-linguistic, so it cannot be directly read or verified by people.

explainer.example: A model solving a multi-step problem passes a continuous vector from one layer to the next instead of writing out an intermediate sentence.
